title: Coral and the Safehouse
premise: Cyrus Halloran, a freelance interpreter who quietly handles the delegations' dirty work, discovers that a decommissioned safehouse he once used has been listed for sale online, its interior photos revealing documents that were supposed to have been destroyed. The listing is bait, set by someone inside the summit's security apparatus to flush out whoever kept copies — and it works. As Cyrus traces the photos back through a chain of brokers, he uncovers a plan to stage an 'accidental' gas explosion at the summit hotel, killing delegates and burying evidence of a secret arms deal. With three days before the summit convenes, Cyrus must decide whether exposing the plot will also expose his own complicity in past cover-ups; in the end he chooses truth over self-preservation, testifying anonymously while letting the safehouse burn with his secrets inside.
about_author: Marguerite Montrose is the pen name of a former conference interpreter who spent a decade working behind glass booths at international summits before turning to fiction. She writes thrillers about the invisible people who keep diplomacy from collapsing.

chapters.title: The Listing
chapters.summary: Cyrus Halloran, scrolling property listings after a sleepless night of post-assignment insomnia, recognizes the interior of Safehouse Kestrel — including a filing cabinet that should have been emptied years ago. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: cold dread disguised as curiosity, the first crack in his carefully compartmentalized life.

chapters.title: Booth Work
chapters.summary: Flashback-tinged chapter establishing Cyrus's role as the interpreter who handles deniable conversations between delegations. He takes a routine contract for the upcoming Meridian Summit and notices security briefings omitting any mention of Kestrel. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: professional detachment beginning to fray as patterns refuse to stay separate.

chapters.title: The Broker Who Sold Silence
chapters.summary: Cyrus tracks the realtor's listing agency to a discreet fixer named Odile Vasseur, who sells discretion to intelligence contractors. Their meeting is polite and lethal; she admits the photos came to her already curated. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: the vertigo of realizing someone wanted him to see the photos.

chapters.title: What Was in the Cabinet
chapters.summary: Cyrus recalls what the cabinet held: transcripts of a private arms negotiation between two summit nations, transcripts he was ordered to destroy and secretly copied instead. His copy is missing from his own archive. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: guilt surfacing — loyalty to the mission versus loyalty to the truth.

chapters.title: An Old Colleague
chapters.summary: Cyrus reaches out to Renata Ilic, a former delegation aide now working summit logistics, under the pretext of contract terms. She warns him off, too quickly, and he notices her hands shaking. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: the loneliness of not knowing who is compromised and who is afraid.

chapters.title: The Man Who Watches Listings
chapters.summary: A surveillance operative, Marcus Teague, is introduced watching Cyrus's apartment; his POV reveals the trap's architecture and that his employer wants Cyrus alive — for now. POV: Teague. Emotional beat: professional unease; Teague suspects his employer's plan exceeds his briefing.

chapters.title: Kestrel, Empty
chapters.summary: Cyrus breaks into the safehouse at night and finds it staged: furniture arranged for photographs, the cabinet empty except for one folder bearing his own codename. Someone knows exactly who he is. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: violation and clarity — this is personal, and it is a summons.

chapters.title: The Summons
chapters.summary: A meeting with the man behind the listing: Deputy Security Director Aldous Wrenn, who offers Cyrus immunity and a role in the summit in exchange for help finding the leaked transcripts. Cyrus recognizes the offer as both genuine threat and genuine fear. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: the seduction of legitimacy versus the smell of rot.

chapters.title: Renata's Ledger
chapters.summary: Renata, cornered by Cyrus, confesses she was ordered to reroute the summit hotel's maintenance contracts to a firm called Halcyon Facilities — a firm with no history. She gives him the ledger and begs him to lose it. POV: Renata. Emotional beat: terror and relief of finally telling someone.

chapters.title: Halcyon Days
chapters.summary: Cyrus investigates Halcyon and finds shell companies, a single employee, and a pending delivery schedule for industrial gas canisters timed forty-eight hours before the summit's opening plenary. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: dread crystallizing into purpose — this is the accident being scheduled.

chapters.title: Teague's Doubt
chapters.summary: Teague is ordered to prepare a 'containment perimeter' around the hotel's service levels and realizes the containment is for witnesses, not threats. He begins quietly documenting his orders. POV: Teague. Emotional beat: a loyal soldier discovering his loyalty has been weaponized against him.

chapters.title: The Interpreter's Ear
chapters.summary: Working a pre-summit bilateral, Cyrus interprets a coded exchange about 'ventilation upgrades' and realizes the attack is meant to look like infrastructure failure, killing the investigation along with the delegates. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: horror translated in real time, forced to speak the words of men planning murder.

chapters.title: Burn Notice
chapters.summary: Wrenn's people ransack Cyrus's apartment searching for his transcript copies; he escapes with only his memory and Renata's ledger, going dark in a dockside hotel. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: stripped bare — everything he built to protect himself is gone but the truth.

chapters.title: Allies of Convenience
chapters.summary: Teague, following protocol breadcrumbs, finds Cyrus instead of arresting him; they trade what each knows and form a wary alliance neither trusts. POV: alternating Cyrus/Teague. Emotional beat: two professionals choosing each other over their institutions.

chapters.title: Renata Taken
chapters.summary: Renata disappears; a staged suicide note appears. Cyrus decodes a detail in the note — a phrase only she would never write — proving she is alive and being held where the operation is run. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: rage sharpened into resolve; no more half-measures.

chapters.title: The Architecture of Accident
chapters.summary: Cyrus and Teague map the hotel's service corridors and gas systems, confirming the detonation method and identifying the trigger window during the opening reception. They need proof that points upward to Wrenn's principal. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: cold clarity — they have hours, not days.

chapters.title: Wrenn's Confession
chapters.summary: Cyrus walks into Wrenn's office wearing a wire, provokes him into implicating his superior, Minister-Counselor Dragan Ferro, then barely escapes when the wire is detected. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: terror and triumph braided together; the recording may be his death warrant or his vindication.

chapters.title: Kestrel Burns
chapters.summary: Ferro's men torch the safehouse to erase the trail, and Cyrus watches his past literally go up in smoke — including the last physical evidence of his own old compromises. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: grief and liberation; the fire frees him because it destroys his reasons for silence.

chapters.title: Forty Minutes
chapters.summary: The climax: Cyrus and Teague infiltrate the hotel's sub-basement during the opening reception, disable the gas manifold, and rescue Renata from a service room, all while Ferro's technicians close in. POV: alternating, converging. Emotional beat: breathless sacrifice — every skill Cyrus ever used for concealment turned toward exposure.

chapters.title: The Recording Plays
chapters.summary: With the attack failed, Cyrus delivers Wrenn's recorded confession to an independent summit oversight panel rather than any national authority, forcing an open inquiry that names Ferro. Teague surrenders himself as a cooperating witness. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: the terrifying relief of stepping into the light.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Cyrus testifies anonymously, walking the line between exposing the plot and confessing his own years of laundering secrets — the panel grants him limited immunity, and Ferro is indicted. Renata, recovering, chooses to testify openly. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: justice outside the law proves imperfect but real.

chapters.title: A New Listing
chapters.summary: Months later, Cyrus finds a modest cottage listed for sale — no secrets in its photos — and makes an offer. Renata visits; something unforced begins. He keeps interpreting, but only for open sessions now. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: quiet earned peace; memory kept, loyalty redefined as truth-telling.
